`codex` is an **agent-runner** provider in this codebase, not chat-completions: `build_provider()` dispatches `provider_id == "codex"` to `CodexProvider(AgentRunnerProvider)` (`scripts/reviewer.py:1548`, dispatch at `scripts/reviewer.py:1777`), and only `anthropic` takes the chat-completions path whose tool loop exposes `set_pr_complexity`. So on this matrix only the `anthropic` leg performs the assessment — `claude-code`, `cursor` **and `codex`** all log the no-op warning (`build_agent_runner_noop_warning`, `scripts/reviewer.py:5245`), exactly as the referenced `docs/PR_METADATA_CHECKS.md` provider table (line 93) states. The PR description repeats the same claim, so the dogfood coverage of the feature is documented as 2 legs when it is 1. A maintainer reading this could later assume `codex` re-labels complexity when the `anthropic` leg is absent.

```suggestion
          # (anthropic) performs the assessment; agent-runner legs
          # (claude-code, cursor, codex) log a no-op warning by design.
```

This citation now misquotes the section it points at: `docs/TRIGGER_MODES.md:64` still heads the recipe "Recipe: run once when labelled `ready`, block merge until it passes". More importantly, the rename isn't mirrored in the docs that instruct how to trigger this workflow — `AGENTS.md:315` still says the dogfood is "label-gated on `ready`". Since this repo's pre-commit checklist requires `self-review.yml` to run on every PR and agents follow `AGENTS.md`, the next agent-driven PR will apply `ready`, the scope gate won't match it, and the self-review will silently never fire. Update `AGENTS.md` and the `TRIGGER_MODES.md` recipe heading in this PR (README.md:318/350 cite the same recipe by its old name), or state the follow-up explicitly.

## Verdict

The change works — both new inputs match the `action.yml` contract (`complexity-labels-enabled` / `complexity-label-prefix` → `AIPRR_COMPLEXITY_LABELS_ENABLED` / `AIPRR_COMPLEXITY_LABEL_PREFIX`), the `ready` → `AIReview` rename is internally consistent across the whole workflow (`no-gate-label`, scope logic, gate `if:`, comments), and both sides of the label match are case-insensitive (the scope job's `tr`+grep and `reviewer.py`'s `label-gate` matching per `tests/test_reviewer.py:779`), so there is no mismatch foot-gun. I also verified the skip-review-label short-circuit (`reviewer.py:6187`) still fires well before the complexity-label block (`reviewer.py:6664`), so the skip path stays side-effect-free. But two documentation errors should be fixed before merge: the new comment misstates which provider legs can actually perform the complexity assessment, and the label rename leaves the repo's own agent-facing trigger docs stale.
